d.a: Distribution and habitat: — The new species is exclusive to the alpine meadows on ophiolitic bedrock of Mount Sandras, within the borders of Muğla / Denizli provinces. Sandras Mountain, located in southwestern Anatolia, represents one of the major centers of plant diversity in Türkiye, characterized by a remarkably high rate of endemism. In recent years, new species continue to be discovered in the area. These species have been discovered near Allium oculisandrasicum. Some of them are as follows: Muscari serpentinicum Yıldırım, Altıoglu & Pirhan in Pirhan et al. (2015: 3), Leopoldia muglaensis (Eker et al. 2020: 268) Eker (2022: 79), and Allium ayhan-toprakii Yıldırım in Özdöl et al. (2022: 233). Allium oculisandrasicum grows in very limited areas of alpine meadows at altitudes of 2115 – 2200 m on Mount Sandras. It is confined to this region and is floristically allied to the East Mediterranean element.
